results.title: Ghana in final talks with Boeing over revival of national airline – Ambassador Smith
results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says negotiations with Boeing over the establishment of a national airline are nearing completion. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews, Mr Smith said the government was working to finalise arrangements to revive the national carrier, with efforts also underway to attract investors to the project. “We are looking for investors. They may invest in this effort. They may get something out of it. What is important for me is the legacy that the President will leave when he's leaving office—that we will have a national flag back in the air. That is important for me,” he said. Mr Smith said there was considerable public interest in the return of a national airline, arguing that many Ghanaians would welcome the opportunity to travel with a carrier bearing the country’s flag.

results.title: ‘Our young people are afraid of their shadows abroad’ – Ambassador Smith
results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says some young Ghanaians living abroad are struggling with difficult conditions, including unemployment and fear, and has urged them to consider returning home with investors to create opportunities. He cited the Ghanaian community in Worcester, Massachusetts, where he estimates about 45,000 Ghanaians live, as an example of the challenges facing members of the diaspora. Speaking in a one-on-one interview with Desmond Danso on JoyNews, Ambassador Smith said some Ghanaians in the city were not working and appeared to live in fear. "I went to Worcester in Massachusetts and there are about 45,000 Ghanaians in Worcester alone. And ask me whether they are working. No. They're not. And they are even afraid of their shadows that the eyes will pick them. So, they are spending most of their time in their churches," he said.

results.title: Government must sustain economic gains and grow productive sector – Ghana’s US Ambassador
results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, says the government has stabilised the economy and is now shifting its focus towards expanding the productive sector. He said the initial priority was to address economic challenges, particularly exchange rate instability and high inflation, before turning attention to sectors that can drive production, investment and job creation. Speaking in a one-on-one interview with Desmond Danso on JoyNews, Ambassador Smith said the government had made progress on economic stabilisation and must now focus on growing productive activities. "The initial thing we did was to stabilise an economy which was in complete mess in terms of our exchange rates and inflation and what have you. We've stabilised it. results.title: Ghana Ambassador to US Victor Smith urges diaspora to attract investment and create jobs
results.content: Ghana's Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, has urged the Ghanaian diaspora to return home with investors to create jobs and opportunities for young people. Speaking in a one-on-one interview with Desmond Danso on JoyNews, Ambassador Smith said he is actively engaging investors in the US to sell the opportunities that exist in Ghana. "Now, that is where I am on the other side of the Atlantic asking us to sell the opportunities that exist to the foreign investors. There are big opportunities in mining, energy, agriculture, you name it, manufacturing," he stated.

results.title: GMA proposes dedicated fund to finance emergency healthcare
results.content: The Ghana Medical Association (GMA) is urging the government to establish a dedicated emergency healthcare fund to ease the financial burden on patients who require urgent medical attention but cannot afford treatment. The proposed fund would ensure that hospitals are compensated for emergency services provided to patients who are unable to pay immediately, particularly in life-threatening situations. Speaking to JoyNews after the Association’s 68th Annual General Conference, the GMA’s General Secretary, Dr Richard Salomey, said the government should consider creating a sustainable funding arrangement to support emergency care. He suggested that part of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) allocation, as well as a percentage of private vehicle insurance premiums, could be considered as potential sources of funding.

results.title: ADB Medicals, Philips advance partnership to introduce medical technology in Ghana
results.content: ADB Ghana Medicals System Group Ltd and global health technology company Philips are moving to implement a strategic partnership to introduce advanced medical equipment and healthcare solutions to Ghana’s health sector. The two companies reaffirmed their commitment to the collaboration during a high-level executive engagement in Accra on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, following the conclusion of a strategic agreement. Discussions focused on implementation preparations, including project governance, operational readiness, equipment deployment arrangements, and outstanding contractual and commercial matters. The engagement was intended to move the partnership from the agreement stage towards implementation, with both companies working to establish the structures needed to deliver the project.

results.title: Rikolto Ghana leads over 200 residents in climate change advocacy march in Asankragwa
results.content: More than 200 residents, including farmers, have marched through Asankragwa in the Wassa Amenfi West District of the Western Region to raise awareness of climate change and its growing impact on farming communities. The march, led by Rikolto Ghana under its Community-Based Adaptation to Climate Change and Advocacy Project (CCAM), brought together participants from 10 project communities, as well as youth and women’s groups, traditional authorities, civil society organisations and government institutions. Representatives of the Forestry Commission and the district’s Agriculture Directorate also took part.
